articleTitle: Research and Analysis of the Effects of Different Shielding Materials on Resisting Side-Channel Attacks on IoT Device Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: The IoT era is witnessing significant growth, with an ever-expanding array of devices finding applications in smart homes, offices, and factories. To link sensors to networks, versatile and lightweight microcontrollers are employed. Unfortunately, this surge in connectivity has given rise to increasingly severe cyber-attacks. In this study, we delve into various materials that can safeguard IoT micro controllers against side-channel attacks. We also propose a specific structure that harnesses electromagnetic energy gaps to craft a frequency-selective surface (FSS). This approach prevents the electromagnetic radiation characteristics of microcontroller encryption processes from leaking, all while ensuring smooth communication within the Wi-Fi frequency band, which enhances resist side-channel attacks.

articleTitle: Research on Voice Traffic Transmitted Over an IP Network Based on IP PBX Asterisk under the Use of Various Codecs and Cryptosystems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: The prevalence of vulnerabilities in telephone networks necessitates the investigation and development of advanced security measures for IP telephony systems. This research focuses on analyzing and enhancing the security of data transmission in Asterisk-based IP telephony systems. We propose a method that combines voice-to-text transcription using the Python Speech Recognition library with the RSA and EI-Gamal asymmetric cryptosystems for encryption and decryption. The study evaluates the time parameters of these cryptosystems to ensure the security of transmitted information. The findings can be applied to optimize secure data transmission for various types of information, including confidential defense-related data and sensitive business information.

articleTitle: A Real-Time Approach to Detecting API Abuses Based on Behavioral Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: Over the past two decades, the internet has undergone a remarkable expansion, giving rise to the development of web-based software solutions. This evolution has led to widespread web Application Programming Interface (API) usage, facilitating remote software communication. However, the increased frequency of API calls has unfortunately resulted in a corresponding surge in API misuse instances. Monitoring API traffic becomes imperative to ensure data security, service availability, and system integrity. This paper introduces an API abuse detection system within a Log Storage Application utilizing Spring Boot with OAuth2.0 and JSON Web Token (JWT) based authentication. The proposed system effectively safeguards against critical security threats, such as Economical Denial of Service (EDoS) attacks (OWASP top 4), Unauthorized Access attempts (OWASP top 3), Brute Force Broken User Authentication, and Behavioral API abuses, with alerts promptly sent to the server. The prevalence of API usage has created numerous attack surfaces, offering a rich landscape for further research opportunities.

articleTitle: Finding Generators of Ideals in Non-Cyclic Number Fields by Using Norm Relations
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: We present a pre-quantum subfield attack of PIP in a non-cyclic fields with pre-processing by using the norm relation. This algorithm reduce the PIP from the original number field to its low dimensional subfields, hence it plays an effect on lattice reduction. At first we describe a new method to find the norm relation. Then we analyse the time complexity of the algorithm. This algorithm can be put in good use in some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(l_{1},\ l_{2},\ \ldots l_{s})$</tex> -type number fields.

articleTitle: A Rapid Fatigue Detection Network for Air Traffic Controller Based on Euler Video Amplification and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: Air traffic controllers play a significant role in ensuring civil aviation safety. Their fatigue state may cause air traffic accidents. In order to provide fast detection of fatigue state, this paper proposed a convolutional neural network with Eulerian video magnification based on controllers' facial data, namely ECNN. ECNN firstly performs Euler detail magnification to mine subtle changes on facial images. Then, an attention mechanism in the subsequent convolution process is added to make the network input focus more facial fatigue feature. Finally, a series experiments collected from several air traffic controllers were implemented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed ECNN. The comparative experiment shows that the Eulerian detail amplification module can effectively improve the convergence speed of the neural network. Comparing with the results obtained by Inception and VGG networks, ECNN has a higher recognition accuracy 98.43 %.

articleTitle: Arbitration Electronic Contract Scheme Based on Blind Signature
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: In order to establish secure and reliable electronic contracts between mutually distrustful parties on the Internet, a blind signature-based arbitration electronic contract scheme is proposed. The contracting parties first establish a shared key using an improved Diffie-Hellman protocol. Then both parties en-crypt the contract using the shared key, which cannot be analyzed or cracked. Finally, each party blinds the contract and submits it to a third-party arbitration institution. After verifying the consistency of the submitted contracts, the arbitration institution applies blind signatures to the blinded contracts and distributes them to the two parties. In case of disputes, the signed contract can be submitted to the arbitration institution for resolution. This scheme ensures the establishment of secure and reliable electronic contracts between mutually distrustful users and provides fast third-party authoritative rulings in case of contract disputes. Furthermore, neither the arbitration institution nor any other third party can access the content of the contract. So this scheme can protect user's privacy effectively.

articleTitle: Tuning Pseudonymization Parameters in a Privacy by Design Approach for Secure Information Discovery Between Federated Organizations
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: Secure and privacy-preserving information discovery between independent organizations is a major challenge in a variety of contexts, such as public authorities (e.g., public security or health authorities) or business cooperation of private organizations. Isolated databases, security and privacy regulations, as well as a lack of trust often hinder an efficient and secure information discovery and information exchange between these entities. To overcome these obstacles, a generic semi-automated hit/no-hit-system for secure information discovery between federated organizations has been developed in a joint research project that is presented in this publication. The distributed system uses a pseudonymization approach allowing for similarity searches between pseudonyms. It has been tested in a pilot phase of the European Police Records Index System (EPRIS) which will become the basis for the new regulation for automated data exchange for police cooperation in the EU. This paper presents the underlying considerations of choosing and tuning the pseudonymization parameters.

articleTitle: WOTS-based Conditional Privacy-preserving Authentication Protocol for VANETs
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: With the development of quantum computing, the present asymmetric crypto schemes could be significantly harmed by quantum algorithms. Hence, we propose a conditional privacy-preserving authentication (CPPA for short) protocol for vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs for short) based on Winternitz-type one-time signature (WOTS for short). In the proposed protocol, a vehicle or a roadside unit can verify the validity of a received message, and any third party cannot retrieve the real identity of the vehicle except the trusted authority. Our proposed CPPA can not only ensure privacy but also achieve related security in VANETs, including authentication, non-repudiation, conditional privacy, un-linkability, resistance to quantum analysis, resistance to impersonation attacks, resistance to modification attacks, resistance to replay attacks, resistance to man-in-the-middle attacks, resistance to stolen verifier table attacks, etc. due to adopting WOTS, our proposed protocol achieves the smaller verification key size and the smaller signature size.

articleTitle: An Approach of Privacy-Preserved PQC-based Cyber-threat Intelligence System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: Cyber-attacks have become high frequency and various events in daily life, which forces organizations changing cyber defense strategy. In order to prevent and defense attacks in time, organizations have to obtain outsourcing information, and sharing cyber-threat intelligence can provide organizations ability to defend ongoing or potential cyber-attacks. However, security and privacy of organizations should be noticed because cyber-threat intelligence is a kind of sensitive data for organizations. We design a privacy-preserved post-quantum cryptosystem-based cyber-threat intelligence system which can not only achieve important security features but resist attacks from quantum computers because of applying post-quantum computing. Moreover, blockchain is utilized to provide backtracking or checking records.

articleTitle: Ransomware Defense Empowered: Deep Learning for Real-Time Family Identification with a Proprietary Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: Ransomware, employing encryption techniques, presents a significant threat by rendering data inaccessible. The emergence of diverse ransomware families has inflicted substantial harm on governments, corporations, and individual users. Despite the proliferation of cyber threats, current solutions often delay in real-time detection and identifying ransomware families at early stages. In response, we introduce FCG-RFD, a benchmark dataset with extensive Function Call Graphs (FCG) for ransomware family detection. The continuous evolution of malware poses challenges to antivirus scanners, necessitating recent and updated datasets. This paper presents a dataset comprising 8,095 samples collected from VirusSamples, Virusshare, VirusSign, the Zoo, MalwareBazaar, along with 8,020 normal files collected from MS Store and Softonic. Benchmark results, utilizing LSTM models on this dataset, demonstrate competitive Fl-Scores of 99.24% aligning with State-of-the-art (SOTA) techniques. The dataset is publicly available<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>Dataset Link: https://figshare.com/s/b2da6a26f927627c6c4f, empowering the research community to test diverse methods for enhanced ran-somware detection capabilities.

articleTitle: A Multi-receiver Certificateless Signcryption (MCLS) Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: In this paper, we substantially modify Hung et al. [1] Anonymous Multi-receiver Certificateless Encryption (AMCLE) scheme to a Multi-receiver Certificateless Signcryption (MCLS) scheme, which provides authentication and introduces public verifiability as an additional feature. We show that, as compared to existing signcryption, our scheme requires less computation for the signcryption and unsigncryption phases. Additionally, the signcryption cost is linear with the number of designated receivers, while the unsigncryption cost remains constant. We compare the results with existing single-receiver and multi-receiver signcryption schemes and show that our proposed MCLS scheme is more efficient for single and multi-receiver signcryption schemes while providing an exemption from the key escrow problem and working in certificateless public key settings.

articleTitle: A Trust Service Model Adaptable to Various Assurance Levels by Linking Digital IDs and Certificates
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: Trust services based on regulations and guidelines such as those provided by eIDAS and NIST SP800-63 are rapidly proceeding toward the realization of sound electronic transactions. The assurance level of the entire service is determined by the assurance level of the trust service provider, identity verification, and authentication. For example, transactions in compliance with the law require identity authentication using digital certificates with a high level of assurance. However, since personal information is required for strict authentication, there is a privacy trade-off. Therefore, it is preferable to have the ability to use different digital certificates for different services depending on the appropriate assurance level and legal requirements. However, there are some practical issues, such as the inability to link services across multiple digital certificates and complexities involved in managing them. Therefore, this study proposes a trust service model that is adaptable to various assurance levels by defining replaceable service components. Specifically, users are issued multiple digital certificates with different assurance levels, which they can link with their digital ID, enabling certificate switching and flexible inter-service collaboration. This study introduces domestic examples based on this model, whereby the scalability of the services is studied in relation to passport identity verification.

articleTitle: An Application Evaluation for Differentially Private Database Release Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: Privacy violations involving de-anonymizing personal identifiable information (PII) due to data mining or breach is a corporate domain concern. Therefore, maintaining individual data anonymity has been challenging due to de-anonymization strategies employed to mine personal data. Counteracting de-anonymization data mining techniques have been deployed where anonymous data is cross-referenced with related data sources to de-anonymize the data source. Subsequently, privacy-enhancing technologies [PETs] have been suggested and deployed in academic and professional to prevent de-anonymization when extracting information from large datasets. Differential privacy (DP) is among the preferred privacy commitments among contemporary privacy models because it guarantees the protection of user-sensitive data. This research evaluates three differentially private database release methods, kernel mean embedding (KME), the learning theory (LT) approach to non-interactive database privacy, and the statistical framework for (SF) differential privacy. This evaluation indicates limitations and provides applicability suggestions for each method to maintain data anonymity and measures to overcome the challenges. Our study provides practitioners with guidelines on the DP selection based on the data nature.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Non-Elliptic Curve Based Primality Tests
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: Modern-day information security depends on implementing Diffie-Hellman, which requires the generation of prime numbers. Because the number of primes is infinite, it is impractical to store prime numbers for use, and therefore, primality tests are indispensable in modern-day information security. A primality test is a test to determine whether a number is prime or composite. There are two types of primality tests, which are deterministic tests and probabilistic tests. Deterministic tests are adopting algorithms that provide a definite answer whether a given number is prime or composite. While in probabilistic tests, a probabilistic result would be provided, there is a degree of uncertainty. In this paper, we review three probabilistic tests: the Fermat Primality Test, the Miller-Rabin Test, and the Baillie-Psw Test, as well as one deterministic test, the Agrawal-Kayal-Saxena (AKS) Test. Furthermore, we do an analysis of these tests. All of the reviews discussed are not based on the Elliptic Curve. The analysis demonstrates that, in the majority of real-world scenarios, the Baillie-Psw test's favorability stems from its typical operational complexity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(log^{3}n)$</tex> and its capacity to deliver accurate results for numbers below 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">64</sup>.

articleTitle: Efficient Active and Concurrent-Secure ID-Based Identification from Digital Signature
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: This paper shows how to transform digital signature (DS) schemes to efficient ID-based identification (IBI) schemes in general. Different from prior works, our transformations do not rely on OR-proof or its variants and thus obtain IBI with better efficiency. More precisely, a transformation from unforgeable DS to IBI which is secure against passive impersonation attack, and a transformation from strongly unforgeable DS to IBI which is secure against active and concurrent impersonation attacks are proposed. We apply the transformations on Katz-Wang signature and obtain an efficient active and concurrent-secure IBI scheme.

articleTitle: PPSC: A Privacy-Preserving Stateless Cryptocurrency System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: Empowered by the blockchain technology, cryptocurrencies have become quite popular in recent years. In account-based cryptocurrency systems, maintaining the state of every account is essential for a node to validate transactions, which generally requires a large storage space. In addition to this efficiency issue, privacy issues in cryptocurrency systems attract people's increasing attention. To address the above issues, this paper proposes a privacy-preserving stateless cryptocurrency system named PPSC. Specifically, PPSC reduces the storage cost of a node by employing the aggregatable sub-vector commitment scheme (aSVC). The node only needs to maintain a commitment of the large state vector. And transactions can be validated in a stateless manner. The aSVC scheme is also utilized to hide the value of a transaction. By utilizing the ring signature scheme, PPSC can hide the sender and the receiver of a transaction from third parties. Simulation results demonstrate that PPSC is space efficient, and the time overhead for privacy preserving is acceptable.

articleTitle: An Image Attribute-Based Approach for Generating Minimally Perturbed Images for Face Concealment
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: Recent advancements in face detection technology have enabled computers to perform more complex tasks; however, this technology also implies a potential increase in malicious activities, such as illegal tracking and surveillance. The exploitability of face detection systems has consequently led to the development of their antithesis: anti-face detection systems. In particular, the Fast Gradient Sign Method -a state-of-the-art adversarial-based solution-is an effective anti-face detection method but comes with the caveat of often perturbing the image more than necessary to thwart face detection systems. Therefore, this study introduces a model that explores Emin, representing the minimum amount of perturbation necessary to cause face detection systems to misdetect using the image attributes of the face region. Our results indicate that faces were effectively concealed at a ratio of 0.7700, which is a significant improvement from a previous study with a concealment ratio of 0.3802. Our method exhibits lower time complexity than a binary search for the minimum perturbation parameter Emin and produces better image quality than naive approaches.

articleTitle: Linkage Deanonymization Risks, Data-Matching and Privacy: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Cryptography, Security and Privacy (CSP)
abstract: Data anonymization is a widely used solution for preserving users' privacy in data publishing. It is achieved through Privacy Preserving Data Publishing (PPDP), which provides a set of models, tools, and methods to defend against the privacy threats. However, data anonymization has been considered insufficient to protect data privacy for years. New de-anonymization techniques increase the risk of breaching privacy protection through data anonymization. Previous researchers write papers on de-anonymization techniques. In most cases, the dataset used for simulation had a limited range and small scale. In this paper, we aim to evaluate the potential of large-scale datasets being vulnerable to linkage attacks with external social media network data. The data set resource comes from the April 2023 Labour Force Survey (Statistics Canada, 2023). The team estimates the probability of successful linkage attacks of a dataset drawn from the entire population with published attributes that could be linked with publicly available data with the same individually specific attributes. The result shows that the estimated deanonymization risks for each of Newfoundland and Labrador, Prince Edward Island, and Manitoba are 12.5%, 12.5% and 1.9% respectively. It can be summarized that de-anonymization risk is inversely proportional to the underlying population size (or number of entries). It is intuitive in that the more diverse the population, the less risk of deanonymization through linkage with selected attributes. Therefore, we conclude that a more extensive scaling and more comprehensive entries dataset decreases the probability of successful linkage de-anonymization attacks.
